blocks.html: A computer cannot think. It only follows instructions — very fast and without mistakes. A program is a set of instructions, written in a fixed order, that tells the computer how to do a task. Writing programs is called programming or coding, and the person who writes them is a programmer.
A programming language is a special language with strict rules (syntax) for writing those instructions.

blocks.html: Before writing code, a programmer plans the steps.
An algorithm is a finite, step-by-step list of instructions to solve a problem.

blocks.text: Example — algorithm to find the total and average of marks in three subjects:

items.html: Start.
Read marks M1, M2, M3.
Total ← M1 + M2 + M3.
Average ← Total ÷ 3.
Print Total and Average.
Stop.

blocks.html: A flowchart is a diagram of an algorithm drawn with standard symbols.
Good algorithms are clear (each step has one meaning), finite (they end) and correct (they give the right answer).

C++ was created by Bjarne Stroustrup at Bell Laboratories, USA. He began in 1979 by adding new features to the C language ("C with Classes"), and the language was named C++ in 1983. The ++ is the C operator for "add one" — so C++ means "one step beyond C".
C++ is used to build operating systems, browsers, games and game engines, banking software, databases and embedded systems. It is fast, powerful and is the foundation for learning other languages.

You need a compiler and an editor, or an IDE (Integrated Development Environment) that combines both. Free choices: Code::Blocks (with the MinGW g++ compiler), Dev-C++, Visual Studio Code with g++, or an online C++ compiler in the browser. Save C++ files with the extension .cpp.

items.html: x++ or ++x adds 1; x-- or --x subtracts 1.
Postfix x++ uses the old value first, then increases. Prefix ++x increases first, then uses the new value.

blocks.html: Relational operators compare two values and give true (1) or false (0): == (equal to),
!= (not equal), > , < , >= , <= .
Logical operators combine conditions: && (AND — both true), || (OR — at least one true), ! (NOT — reverses).

blocks.html: Finding and fixing errors is called debugging.

Did you know? The word "bug" became popular after engineers in 1947 found a real moth stuck in a relay of the Harvard Mark II computer. They taped it into their logbook as the "first actual case of bug being found".
Aim: To install a C++ compiler, write, compile and run programs, and fix errors.

items.html: Set up. Install Code::Blocks (the version that includes MinGW) or open an online C++ compiler.
Hello program. Create hello.cpp , type Program 10.1 (do not copy-paste), and click Build and Run (F9 in Code::Blocks).
Make it yours. Change the message to print your name, class and school on three lines.
Break it on purpose. Remove one semicolon and build again. Read the error message and note the line number. Fix it. Then change cout to Cout and see what happens.
Input and output. Type Program 10.3 and run it with three different pairs of numbers.
Integer division. In Program 10.7, change a to 20 and b to 6. Predict each output before running; then check.
Logical error hunt. Write a program to find the average of three numbers. Deliberately write a + b + c / 3 , run it with 10, 20, 30 and explain why the answer (40) is wrong. Fix it to get 20.
